acceptance: read() stops writing revs/ and `last`; legacy snapshot folders are reclaimed only by the explicit `todo-db cache prune`, never inside read().
The snapshot cache is a bare git object store per namespace (<cache>/<ns>/store.git) fetched incrementally by URL with no configured remote; reads build snapshots from objects.
refs/todo-db/tip replaces the `last` pointer and is updated by compare-and-swap; it never moves back to an ancestor, and follows a divergent remote rewrite.
Store growth after maintenance is at most 2x the raw bytes of the items touched, and unpacked slack between maintenance runs is capped (8 MiB), enforced by a detached, locked repack -A + prune.
mutate, restore_rev, read_rev, history and reconcile run against the store; plumbing-built commits match the worktree path in tree OID and commit body.
Offline reads serve the store tip, falling back to legacy revs/<last> until the store has a tip.
`todo-db cache prune` removes legacy revs/, last files, stale tmp files, 40-hex dirs and unused namespaces, and runs maintenance.
Multi-process tests cover concurrent reads and mutations during maintenance, offline reads after maintenance, and the size bound.
Git >= 2.28 is required (already needed by bootstrap).
context: Implemented on branch feat/git-object-store-cache, draft PR https://github.com/joeharris76/todo-db/pull/48 (commits 1ebcc4b, 17fa20a, 280c08d). 228 tests pass. Measured: BenchBox store 14.7 MiB for full history; growth 0.21x (fixture) to 0.58x (BenchBox copy) of item bytes touched; 10k-item publish 3.3s -> 0.41s. The planned in-read eviction stopgap was folded in: read() no longer writes revs/, so there is nothing to evict. Remaining: review and merge PR 48, release, then run `todo-db cache prune` on each machine. Finish this item after merge.
description:
read() caches every new state-branch tip as a full snapshot under <cache>/<ns>/revs/<sha>/ and never deletes old ones. Only the resolved tip and the rev named by `last` are ever read back, so the rest is dead weight. The BenchBox namespace (e688dcd1868ed3f8) held 1,508 revs, about 40 GiB, on 2026-10-16 and grows by up to about 3 GiB a day.

An adversarial review rejected the first proposal (keep only the new tip and the previous `last`): the first sweep would delete ~40 GiB inside read() and exceed the git and MCP timeouts; `last` is written by every process and is not monotonic, so the rule can delete the true newest tip; deleting a rev while another process is in save_snapshot raises a raw FileNotFoundError out of read(); _offline_cached has no fallback for a missing or partial rev.
